## Effect of Treatment With SB 242784 on Soft Tissue Calcification in Rats Treated With Vitamin D

| Tissue, umol    | Vitamin D Only   | Vitamin D+10 mg SB 242784   | Vitamin D+40 mg SB 242784   | Age-Matched Control   |
|-----------------|------------------|-----------------------------|-----------------------------|-----------------------|
| Abdominal aorta | 3.1+1.3          | 1.4+0.5*                    | 0.3+0.03t                   | 0.3+0.02              |
| Kidney          | 39.6+32.5        | 20.7+11.9                   |                             | 1.1+0.2               |
| Lungs           | 95.5+24.3        | 26.7+33.6                   | 3.8+0.38                    | 3.4+0.5               |
| Trachea         | 2.0+0.2          |                             | 0.9+0.7/                    | 0.6+0.2               |

Seven-week-old male rats received subcutaneous injections of 500'000 IU of vitamin Dlkg body wt at t=0, 24, and 48 hours. Subsets of these animals were also injected with either 10 or 40 mg SB 242784/kg body wt per beginning at 2 days before the first injection of vitamin D. Animals were killed 96 hours after the first vitamin D injection; and the abdominal aorta; one kidney, the lungs; and an anatomically uniform 1 cm of trachea were ashed (see Materials and Methods for further details) . The ashed tissues were extracted with acid to dissolve minerals, and each acid extract was analyzed for calcium as described in Materials and tissues analyzed.  Therefore; the increase in calcium content seen in the tissues from the vitamin D treatment group cannot be due to changes in the size or mass day

Data are mean+SD, n=4, for all groups.

*P=0.06 compared with vitamin D only.

#P=0.063 compared with vitamin D only.

SP=0.0003 compared with vitamin D only.

IlP=0.023 compared with vitamin D only.

control animals (Table) Calcium levels measured on serum obtained 96 hours after the first vitamin D injection were as (n=4), 14.0+0.9 for rats treated vitamin D plus the dose of SB 242784 (n=4) (P>0.5 versus vitamin with vitamin D plus the versus vitamin D alone), and 10.9+0.3 for untreated control mgldL with 10-mg 40-mg mg/dL

To confirm that SB 242784 did in fact inhibit bone resorption at the doses used in the above experiments; serum samples  obtained at death were analyzed to determine the level of cross-linked N-teleopeptides; specific marker for bone resorption activity that is released the osteoclast mediated breakdown of bone matrix collagen. As seen in Figure 4, the level of cross-linked N-teleopeptides was elevated by 140% in rats treated with vitamin D alone and was   reduced to below control levels in rats treated with vitamin D plus the higher dose of SB 242784. This result during arterial calcification   by accelerating bone   resorption and shows that SB 242784 treatment dose-dependently inhibits bone resorption activity in the vitamin D-treated rat.

<!-- image -->

The effect of SB 242784 on arterial calcification was also examined in rats treated with warfarin, treatment that inactivates the calcification-inhibitory activity of matrix Gla protein and thereby induces calcification of arteries and cartilage. In the first experiment; weanling rats were treated for week with warfarin alone or with warfarin plus 10 mg SB 242784/kg per This   experiment showed that  the dose of SB 242784 did not significantly inhibit arterial calcification as assessed by alizarin red staining. Subsequent analysis of bone resorption activity the  cross-linked N-teleopeptide   assay showed that   the dose of SB 242784 also did not  significantly   reduce bone resorption activity in the warfarin-treated  rats. When this experiment was repeated at the higher dose (40 mg/kg per of SB 242784, we observed that the strongly inhibited arterial rapid day . 10-mg using 10-mg day) drug

Figure 4. Effect of SB 242784 on bone resorption activity as measured by serum cross-linked N-teleopeptides. Serum was obtained from each animal 96 hours after the first vitamin D injection in the experiment described in the Figure legend, and serum was also obtained from age-matched control rats. Each serum sample was analyzed to determine the level of cross-linked N-teleopeptides (OSTEOMARK NTx, Ostex) , specific marker for bone resorption activity (see Materials and Methods). Results are presented as meanSD a, P<0.01 compared with control; b, P<0.05 compared with vitamin D only; and c, P<0.0O1 compared with vitamin D only.
